When Venus is brightest, and why it is flat

Greatest brilliancy, properly called greatest illuminated extent, is the moment the lit area of Venus’s disc as seen from Earth is largest. Since Venus passed between us and the Sun on October 23, it has been pulling away: the disc shrinks each week as the distance grows, while the sunlit fraction grows as the angle opens. The product of the two, the actual area of lit planet, rises to a maximum and then falls. ultimate.title: Spot Venus at Peak Brightness for 2026
ultimate.snippet:
By Konstantin Bikos

Published 10-Sep-2026. Updated 29-Oct-2026

## A Celestial Show for Early Birds

On its orbit around the Sun, Venus will soon be swinging into prime position for Earthly stargazers. The planet will reach peak brightness in late November, when it will shine just before sunrise as the “Morning Star.”

Best Time to Spot Venus in 2026

Venus will reach peak brightness on November 27, 2026.

With an apparent magnitude of −4.87, the planet will shine more than 20 times brighter than Sirius, the brightest star in the sky.

While it will be visible in the pre-dawn sky from both hemispheres, northern observers will have a slightly better vantage point to view the spectacle as Venus will be above the horizon well before sunrise; south of the equator, it will first become visible during morning twilight, especially in the far south.

See how it will look in New York, USA, and Sydney, Australia.

...

## Brightest During the Crescent Phase

The two moments of peak brightness occur on either side of Venus’s inferior conjunction on October 24, 2026, the moment when it passes (roughly) between Earth and the Sun. See what happens when it aligns perfectly.

For a few days around this date, Venus disappears from view entirely as it is swallowed by the Sun’s glare.

In the weeks before and after, however, we view Venus from an angle that makes a small portion of its illuminated side visible to us. In other words, we’re looking at Venus’s crescent phases—waning in September and waxing in November.

These are the moments the planet reaches peak brightness in the sky.
